sanskrit: vistarāḥ kleśasaṃyuktāḥ saṃkṣepās tu sukhāvahāḥ parārthaṃ vistarāḥ sarve tyāgam ātmahitaṃ viduḥ
english: Elaborate undertakings are bound up with toil, while the simple ones bring ease; all elaborate striving is for the sake of others, but the wise know renunciation to be one's own true good.

sanskrit: saṃkalpajo mitravargo jñātayaḥ kāraṇātmakāḥ bhāryā dāsāś ca putrāś ca svam artham anuyuñjate
english: The circle of friends is born of intention, and kinsmen are bound by self-interest; wife, servants, and sons alike pursue each their own advantage.

sanskrit: na mātā na pitā kiṃ cit kasya cit pratipadyate dānapathyodano jantuḥ svakarmaphalam aśnute
english: Neither mother nor father can take on aught for another; the creature, whose only provision for the road is what it has given, feeds on the fruit of its own deeds alone.

sanskrit: mātā putraḥ pitā bhrātā bhāryā mitrajanas tathā aṣṭāpadapadasthāne tv akṣamudreva nyasyate
english: Mother, son, father, brother, wife, and friends are set down upon the squares of life's board like dice cast at their stations on the gaming-cloth.

sanskrit: sarvāṇi karmāṇi purā kṛtāni; śubhāśubhāny ātmano yānti jantoḥ upasthitaṃ karmaphalaṃ viditvā; buddhiṃ tathā codayate 'ntarātmā
english: All the deeds a creature has wrought of old, good and evil, follow after the self; and the inner soul, perceiving that the fruit of deeds has come upon it, accordingly spurs the intellect to act.

sanskrit: vyavasāyaṃ samāśritya sahāyān yo 'dhigacchati na tasya kaś cid ārambhaḥ kadā cid avasīdati
english: He who, taking his stand upon resolve, gains himself helpers—no enterprise of his ever sinks into failure.

sanskrit: advaidhamanasaṃ yuktaṃ śūraṃ dhīraṃ vipaścitam na śrīḥ saṃtyajate nityam ādityam iva raśmayaḥ
english: The man of undivided mind, steadfast, brave, resolute, and wise—prosperity never forsakes him, even as its rays never forsake the sun.

sanskrit: āstikyavyavasāyābhyām upāyād vismayād dhiyā yam ārabhaty anindyātmā na so 'rthaḥ parisīdati
english: What the man of blameless soul undertakes with faith and resolve, with skillful means, with wonder, and with wisdom—that aim of his never comes to ruin.

sanskrit: sarvaḥ svāni śubhāśubhāni niyataṃ karmāṇi jantuḥ svayaṃ; garbhāt saṃpratipadyate tad ubhayaṃ yat tena pūrvaṃ kṛtam mṛtyuś cāparihāravān samagatiḥ kālena viccheditā; dāroś cūrṇam ivāśmasāravihitaṃ karmāntikaṃ prāpayet
english: Every creature, fixed by destiny, takes up of itself from the womb its own deeds, both fair and foul—both that which it has formerly wrought; and death, not to be escaped, walking evenly toward all, severed at the appointed time, brings the creature to the end of its deeds, as iron tools reduce a log to dust.

sanskrit: svarūpatām ātmakṛtaṃ ca vistaraṃ; kulānvayaṃ dravyasamṛddhisaṃcayam naro hi sarvo labhate yathākṛtaṃ; śubhāśubhenātmakṛtena karmaṇā
english: His native form, his own self-wrought course of life, his lineage and descent, his hoarded store of wealth—every man obtains all this as he has made it, by the good or evil deeds himself has done.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity ukto janako rājan yathātathyaṃ manīṣiṇā śrutvā dharmavidāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ parāṃ mudam avāpa ha
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed in accordance with truth by that sage, O king, Janaka, foremost among those who know dharma, hearing it, attained the highest joy.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca satyaṃ kṣamāṃ damaṃ prajñāṃ praśaṃsanti pitāmaha vidvāṃso manujā loke katham etan mataṃ tava
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Truth, forbearance, self-restraint, and wisdom—these the learned among men extol in the world, O grandsire. What is your judgment in this matter?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣye 'ham itihāsaṃ purātanam sādhyānām iha saṃvādaṃ haṃsasya ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: On this I shall relate to you an ancient tale, the dialogue here between the Sādhyas and the Swan, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: haṃso bhūtvātha sauvarṇas tv ajo nityaḥ prajāpatiḥ sa vai paryeti lokāṃs trīn atha sādhyān upāgamat
english: Becoming a golden swan, the Unborn, the Eternal, Prajāpati went his rounds through the three worlds, and so he came to the Sādhyas.

sanskrit: sādhyā ūcuḥ śakune vayaṃ sma devā vai sādhyās tvām anuyujmahe pṛcchāmas tvāṃ mokṣadharmaṃ bhavāṃś ca kila mokṣavit
english: The Sādhyas said: O bird, we are gods, the Sādhyas, and we entreat you; we ask of you the dharma of liberation, for you, it is said, are a knower of liberation.

sanskrit: śruto 'si naḥ paṇḍito dhīravādī; sādhuśabdaḥ patate te patatrin kiṃ manyase śreṣṭhatamaṃ dvija tvaṃ; kasmin manas te ramate mahātman
english: We have heard you are learned and a speaker of steady wisdom; the fame of your good name flies abroad, O winged one. What do you deem the highest, O twice-born? In what does your mind take its delight, O great-souled one?

sanskrit: tan naḥ kāryaṃ pakṣivara praśādhi; yat kāryāṇāṃ manyase śreṣṭham ekam yat kṛtvā vai puruṣaḥ sarvabandhair; vimucyate vihagendreha śīghram
english: Teach us then our task, O best of birds—that one work which you deem foremost of all works, by doing which a man is here set free, and swiftly, from all bonds, O king of birds.

sanskrit: haṃsa uvāca idaṃ kāryam amṛtāśāḥ śṛṇomi; tapo damaḥ satyam ātmābhiguptiḥ granthīn vimucya hṛdayasya sarvān; priyāpriye svaṃ vaśam ānayīta
english: The Swan said: This is the task, O you who hope for immortality, as I have learned it—austerity, self-restraint, truth, and guarding of the self; loosing all the knots of the heart, one should bring the pleasant and the unpleasant alike under one's own control.

sanskrit: nāruṃtudaḥ syān na nṛśaṃsavādī; na hīnataḥ param abhyādadīta yayāsya vācā para udvijeta; na tāṃ vaded ruśatīṃ pāpalokyām
english: Let a man not be a stinger to the quick, nor a speaker of cruel words; let him not snatch from another by base means. That speech by which another would be made to shudder—galling and leading to evil worlds—let him not utter it.

sanskrit: vāksāyakā vadanān niṣpatanti; yair āhataḥ śocati rātryahāni parasya nāmarmasu te patanti; tān paṇḍito nāvasṛjet pareṣu
english: Arrows of speech fly forth from the mouth, struck by which a man grieves through nights and days; they fall upon another's tender places—those the wise man should never loose against others.

sanskrit: paraś ced enam ativādabāṇair; bhṛśaṃ vidhyec chama eveha kāryaḥ saṃroṣyamāṇaḥ pratimṛṣyate yaḥ; sa ādatte sukṛtaṃ vai parasya
english: If another should pierce him sorely with the arrows of abusive speech, calm alone should be his course here below; he who, being provoked to wrath, yet endures it, takes to himself the very merit of the other.

sanskrit: kṣepābhimānād abhiṣaṅgavyalīkaṃ; nigṛhṇāti jvalitaṃ yaś ca manyum aduṣṭacetā mudito 'nasūyuḥ; sa ādatte sukṛtaṃ vai pareṣām
english: He who, when stung by insult and pride and the falseness of assault, restrains his blazing anger—untainted in mind, cheerful, free of malice—he takes to himself the merit of others.

sanskrit: ākruśyamāno na vadāmi kiṃ cit; kṣamāmy ahaṃ tāḍyamānaś ca nityam śreṣṭhaṃ hy etat kṣamam apy āhur āryāḥ; satyaṃ tathaivārjavam ānṛśaṃsyam
english: Though reviled, I say nothing; though struck, I ever forbear; for the noble declare forbearance to be the best, and likewise truth, uprightness, and freedom from cruelty.

sanskrit: vedasyopaniṣat satyaṃ satyasyopaniṣad damaḥ damasyopaniṣan mokṣa etat sarvānuśāsanam
english: The secret essence of the Veda is truth; the secret essence of truth is self-restraint; the secret essence of self-restraint is liberation—this is the whole of the teaching.

sanskrit: vāco vegaṃ manasaḥ krodhavegaṃ; vivitsāvegam udaropasthavegam etān vegān yo viṣahaty udīrṇāṃs; taṃ manye 'haṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vai muniṃ ca
english: The urge of speech, the urge of the mind, the urge of anger, the urge of craving, the urges of belly and loins—he who withstands these urges when they rise up, him I deem truly a brāhmaṇa and a sage.

sanskrit: akrodhanaḥ krudhyatāṃ vai viśiṣṭas; tathā titikṣur atitikṣor viśiṣṭaḥ amānuṣān mānuṣo vai viśiṣṭas; tathājñānāj jñānavān vai pradhānaḥ
english: The man free of anger is superior to the angry; the patient is superior to the impatient; the truly human is superior to the brutish; and the man of knowledge is foremost above the ignorant.

sanskrit: ākruśyamāno nākrośen manyur eva titikṣataḥ ākroṣṭāraṃ nirdahati sukṛtaṃ cāsya vindati
english: Though reviled, let him not revile in return; the very anger of the patient man burns up the reviler, and the patient one wins the merit that was his.

sanskrit: yo nātyuktaḥ prāha rūkṣaṃ priyaṃ vā; yo vā hato na pratihanti dhairyāt pāpaṃ ca yo necchati tasya hantus; tasmai devāḥ spṛhayante sadaiva
english: He who, though heavily abused, speaks neither harsh word nor flattering one; who, though struck, strikes not back out of steadfastness; and who wishes no evil to him that smites him—for such a man the gods ever yearn.

sanskrit: pāpīyasaḥ kṣametaiva śreyasaḥ sadṛśasya ca vimānito hato ''kruṣṭa evaṃ siddhiṃ gamiṣyati
english: Let one forbear toward the worse, the better, and the equal alike; slighted, struck, and reviled, thus shall he attain perfection.

sanskrit: sadāham āryān nibhṛto 'py upāse; na me vivitsā na ca me 'sti roṣaḥ na cāpy ahaṃ lipsamānaḥ paraimi; na caiva kiṃ cid viṣameṇa yāmi
english: Ever, though lowly, I wait upon the noble; I have no craving, nor is there any anger in me; nor do I go about grasping after gain, nor do I tread any crooked path at all.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ śaptaḥ pratiśapāmi kiṃ cid; damaṃ dvāraṃ hy amṛtasyeha vedmi guhyaṃ brahma tad idaṃ vo bravīmi; na mānuṣāc chreṣṭhataraṃ hi kiṃ cit
english: Though cursed, I curse not back at all; for I know self-restraint to be the very gate of immortality here. This secret brahman I declare to you: there is nothing higher than the truly human.

sanskrit: vimucyamānaḥ pāpebhyo dhanebhya iva candramāḥ virajāḥ kālam ākāṅkṣan dhīro dhairyeṇa sidhyati
english: Freeing himself from sins as the moon emerges from the clouds, the steadfast man, stainless and awaiting his time, attains perfection through steadfastness.

sanskrit: yaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhavati hy arcanīya; utsecane stambha ivābhijātaḥ yasmai vācaṃ supraśastāṃ vadanti; sa vai devān gacchati saṃyatātmā
english: He who is worthy of all men's worship, like a well-set pillar at a consecration; he of whom men speak words of high praise—he, his self subdued, goes indeed to the gods.

sanskrit: na tathā vaktum icchanti kalyāṇān puruṣe guṇān yathaiṣāṃ vaktum icchanti nairguṇyam anuyuñjakāḥ
english: Men do not so wish to speak of the good qualities in a man as carping fault-finders wish to speak of his lack of worth.

sanskrit: yasya vāṅmanasī gupte samyak praṇihite sadā vedās tapaś ca tyāgaś ca sa idaṃ sarvam āpnuyāt
english: He whose speech and mind are guarded, ever rightly composed—the Vedas, austerity, and renunciation are his; he would attain all this.

sanskrit: ākrośanāvamānābhyām abudhād vardhate budhaḥ tasmān na vardhayed anyaṃ na cātmānaṃ vihiṃsayet
english: By the reviling and contempt of the foolish, the wise man grows; therefore let him not magnify another in retort, nor do violence to his own self.

sanskrit: amṛtasyeva saṃtṛpyed avamānasya vai dvijaḥ sukhaṃ hy avamataḥ śete yo 'vamantā sa naśyati
english: Let the twice-born be content with contempt as though with nectar; for he who is despised sleeps in peace, while he who despises perishes.

sanskrit: yat krodhano yajate yad dadāti; yad vā tapas tapyati yaj juhoti vaivasvatas tad dharate 'sya sarvaṃ; moghaḥ śramo bhavati krodhanasya
english: Whatever sacrifice the angry man offers, whatever he gives, whatever austerity he practices, whatever he pours in oblation—Yama, son of Vivasvat, carries it all away from him; the toil of the angry man is in vain.

sanskrit: catvāri yasya dvārāṇi suguptāny amarottamāḥ upastham udaraṃ hastau vāk caturthī sa dharmavit
english: He whose four gates are well guarded, O best of immortals—the loins, the belly, the hands, and speech as the fourth—he is a knower of dharma.

sanskrit: satyaṃ damaṃ hy ārjavam ānṛśaṃsyaṃ; dhṛtiṃ titikṣām abhisevamānaḥ svādhyāyanityo 'spṛhayan pareṣām; ekāntaśīly ūrdhvagatir bhavet saḥ
english: Devoted to truth, self-restraint, uprightness, and freedom from cruelty, to firmness and to patience; ever given to sacred study, coveting nothing of others, fond of solitude—such a man attains the upward path.

sanskrit: sarvān etān anucaran vatsavac caturaḥ stanān na pāvanatamaṃ kiṃ cit satyād adhyagamaṃ kva cit
english: Pursuing all these as a calf pursues the four teats, nowhere have I ever found anything more purifying than truth.

sanskrit: ācakṣe 'haṃ manuṣyebhyo devebhyaḥ pratisaṃcaran satyaṃ svargasya sopānaṃ pārāvārasya naur iva
english: Moving to and fro among men and gods, I declare it: truth is the stairway to heaven, even as a boat for crossing from shore to shore.

sanskrit: yādṛśaiḥ saṃnivasati yādṛśāṃś copasevate yādṛg icchec ca bhavituṃ tādṛg bhavati pūruṣaḥ
english: With what sort of men a man dwells, what sort he attends upon, and what sort he wishes to become—of that sort the man becomes.

sanskrit: yadi santaṃ sevate yady asantaṃ; tapasvinaṃ yadi vā stenam eva vāso yathā raṅgavaśaṃ prayāti; tathā sa teṣāṃ vaśam abhyupaiti
english: Whether he serves the good or the wicked, whether the ascetic or the thief, as a cloth takes on the color of its dye, so he passes under the sway of those he keeps.

sanskrit: sadā devāḥ sādhubhiḥ saṃvadante; na mānuṣaṃ viṣayaṃ yānti draṣṭum nenduḥ samaḥ syād asamo hi vāyur; uccāvacaṃ viṣayaṃ yaḥ sa veda
english: The gods ever converse with the good; they do not come to look upon the realm of men. Let one be like the moon, even and serene, not like the restless wind—he who knows the realm of high and low.

sanskrit: aduṣṭaṃ vartamāne tu hṛdayāntarapūruṣe tenaiva devāḥ prīyante satāṃ mārgasthitena vai
english: When the inner person within the heart abides untainted, by that very thing are the gods pleased—by one who stands firm upon the path of the good.

sanskrit: śiśnodare ye 'bhiratāḥ sadaiva; stenā narā vākparuṣāś ca nityam apetadoṣān iti tān viditvā; dūrād devāḥ saṃparivarjayanti
english: Those men who are ever given over to the loins and belly, thieves, and harsh of speech without cease—knowing them to be devoid of virtue, the gods shun them from afar.

sanskrit: na vai devā hīnasattvena toṣyāḥ; sarvāśinā duṣkṛtakarmaṇā vā satyavratā ye tu narāḥ kṛtajñā; dharme ratās taiḥ saha saṃbhajante
english: The gods are not to be pleased by the man of base nature, who eats all things and does evil deeds; but with those men vowed to truth, grateful, and delighting in dharma, they hold communion.

sanskrit: avyāhṛtaṃ vyāhṛtāc chreya āhuḥ; satyaṃ vaded vyāhṛtaṃ tad dvitīyam dharmaṃ vaded vyāhṛtaṃ tat tṛtīyaṃ; priyaṃ vaded vyāhṛtaṃ tac caturtham
english: Silence, they say, is better than speech; if one must speak, let him speak the truth—that is the second; let him speak what is in keeping with dharma—that is the third; let him speak what is pleasant—that is the fourth.

sanskrit: sādhyā ūcuḥ kenāyam āvṛto lokaḥ kena vā na prakāśate kena tyajati mitrāṇi kena svargaṃ na gacchati
english: The Sādhyas said: By what is this world enveloped? By what does it fail to shine forth? By what does a man forsake his friends? By what does he fail to reach heaven?

sanskrit: haṃsa uvāca ajñānenāvṛto loko mātsaryān na prakāśate lobhāt tyajati mitrāṇi saṅgāt svargaṃ na gacchati
english: The Swan said: By ignorance is the world enveloped; through envy it fails to shine forth; through greed a man forsakes his friends; through attachment he fails to reach heaven.

sanskrit: sādhyā ūcuḥ kaḥ svid eko ramate brāhmaṇānāṃ; kaḥ svid eko bahubhir joṣam āste kaḥ svid eko balavān durbalo 'pi; kaḥ svid eṣāṃ kalahaṃ nānvavaiti
english: The Sādhyas said: Who, then, among brāhmaṇas takes delight alone? Who, alone, sits content amid many? Who, alone, is strong even though weak? And who among them does not pursue a quarrel?

sanskrit: haṃsa uvāca prājña eko ramate brāhmaṇānāṃ; prājña eko bahubhir joṣam āste prājña eko balavān durbalo 'pi; prājña eṣāṃ kalahaṃ nānvavaiti
english: The Swan said: The wise man among brāhmaṇas takes delight alone; the wise man, alone, sits content amid many; the wise man, alone, is strong even though weak; the wise man among them does not pursue a quarrel.

sanskrit: sādhyā ūcuḥ kiṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ devatvaṃ kiṃ ca sādhutvam ucyate asādhutvaṃ ca kiṃ teṣāṃ kim eṣāṃ mānuṣaṃ matam
english: The Sādhyas said: What is the godhood of brāhmaṇas, and what is called their goodness? What is their badness, and what is held to be the merely human in them?

sanskrit: haṃsa uvāca svādhyāya eṣāṃ devatvaṃ vrataṃ sādhutvam ucyate asādhutvaṃ parīvādo mṛtyur mānuṣam ucyate
english: The Swan said: Sacred study is their godhood; the keeping of vows is called their goodness; slander is their badness; and death is said to be the merely human in them.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca saṃvāda ity ayaṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sādhyānāṃ parikīrtitaḥ kṣetraṃ vai karmaṇāṃ yoniḥ sadbhāvaḥ satyam ucyate
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus has this excellent dialogue of the Sādhyas been recounted. The field is verily the womb of deeds; goodness of being is called truth.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sāṃkhye yoge ca me tāta viśeṣaṃ vaktum arhasi tava sarvajña sarvaṃ hi viditaṃ kurusattama
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of Sāṃkhya and Yoga, dear sire, you should tell me the distinction; for to you, the all-knowing, all is known, O best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sāṃkhyāḥ sāṃkhyaṃ praśaṃsanti yogā yogaṃ dvijātayaḥ vadanti kāraṇaiḥ śraiṣṭhyaṃ svapakṣodbhāvanāya vai
english: Bhīṣma said: The followers of Sāṃkhya extol Sāṃkhya, and the twice-born adherents of Yoga extol Yoga; each declares the superiority of his own by reasons, to exalt his own side.

sanskrit: anīśvaraḥ kathaṃ mucyed ity evaṃ śatrukarśana vadanti kāraṇaiḥ śraiṣṭhyaṃ yogāḥ samyaṅ manīṣiṇaḥ
english: "How could one without a Lord be liberated?"—thus, O harrier of foes, the followers of Yoga, well-reasoning sages, declare their superiority by their arguments.

sanskrit: vadanti kāraṇaṃ cedaṃ sāṃkhyāḥ samyag dvijātayaḥ vijñāyeha gatīḥ sarvā virakto viṣayeṣu yaḥ
english: And this reasoning the twice-born followers of Sāṃkhya rightly declare: he who, having understood here all the conditions of being, has grown detached from the objects of sense—

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ sa dehāt suvyaktaṃ vimucyed iti nānyathā etad āhur mahāprājñāḥ sāṃkhyaṃ vai mokṣadarśanam
english: —he, upon rising above the body, is most surely liberated, and not otherwise. This the greatly wise declare to be the Sāṃkhya, the very vision of liberation.

sanskrit: svapakṣe kāraṇaṃ grāhyaṃ samarthaṃ vacanaṃ hitam śiṣṭānāṃ hi mataṃ grāhyaṃ tvadvidhaiḥ śiṣṭasaṃmataiḥ
english: In support of one's own position the reasoning to be accepted is that which is cogent, sound, and salutary; for the judgment of the learned is to be accepted by such as you, esteemed among the learned.

sanskrit: pratyakṣahetavo yogāḥ sāṃkhyāḥ śāstraviniścayāḥ ubhe caite mate tattve mama tāta yudhiṣṭhira
english: The Yogas rest upon direct perception as their ground, the Sāṃkhyas upon the conclusions of scripture; both these doctrines are, in my view, truth, dear Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: ubhe caite mate jñāne nṛpate śiṣṭasaṃmate anuṣṭhite yathāśāstraṃ nayetāṃ paramāṃ gatim
english: Both these doctrines, O king, are held to be true knowledge, approved by the learned; practiced according to scripture, they lead to the supreme goal.

sanskrit: tulyaṃ śaucaṃ tayor yuktaṃ dayā bhūteṣu cānagha vratānāṃ dhāraṇaṃ tulyaṃ darśanaṃ na samaṃ tayoḥ
english: Equal in both is the purity enjoined, and equal the compassion toward all beings, O sinless one; equal is the upholding of vows—but their doctrines of how to see are not the same.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yadi tulyaṃ vrataṃ śaucaṃ dayā cātra pitāmaha tulyaṃ na darśanaṃ kasmāt tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: If vow, purity, and compassion are equal in both here, O grandsire, then why is their doctrine of seeing not the same? Tell me that, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca rāgaṃ mohaṃ tathā snehaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca kevalam yogāc chittvādito doṣān pañcaitān prāpnuvanti tat
english: Bhīṣma said: Passion, delusion, attachment, desire, and anger alone—cutting off from the very start these five faults by means of Yoga, the yogins attain that goal.

sanskrit: yathā cānimiṣāḥ sthūlā jālaṃ chittvā punar jalam prāpnuvanti tathā yogās tat padaṃ vītakalmaṣāḥ
english: As great fishes, breaking the net, win the water again, so the yogins, freed of taint, attain that abode.

sanskrit: tathaiva vāgurāṃ chittvā balavanto yathā mṛgāḥ prāpnuyur vimalaṃ mārgaṃ vimuktāḥ sarvabandhanaiḥ
english: And just as strong beasts, breaking through the snare, would gain the open road, set free from every bond—

sanskrit: lobhajāni tathā rājan bandhanāni balānvitāḥ chittvā yogāḥ paraṃ mārgaṃ gacchanti vimalāḥ śivam
english: —so, O king, the yogins, endowed with strength, breaking the bonds born of greed, go stainless along the supreme and blessed path.

sanskrit: abalāś ca mṛgā rājan vāgurāsu tathāpare vinaśyanti na saṃdehas tadvad yogabalād ṛte
english: But weak beasts, O king, and others caught in the snares perish, beyond doubt; just so do men perish who are without the strength of Yoga.

sanskrit: balahīnāś ca kaunteya yathā jālagatā jhaṣāḥ antaṃ gacchanti rājendra tathā yogāḥ sudurbalāḥ
english: And as feeble fishes caught in the net, O son of Kuntī, come to their end, O lord of kings, so do the very weak among yogins.

sanskrit: yathā ca śakunāḥ sūkṣmāḥ prāpya jālam ariṃdama tatra saktā vipadyante mucyante ca balānvitāḥ
english: And as small birds, falling upon a net, O subduer of foes, caught fast therein come to ruin, while the strong win free—

sanskrit: karmajair bandhanair baddhās tadvad yogāḥ paraṃtapa abalā vai vinaśyanti mucyante ca balānvitāḥ
english: —so, bound by the bonds born of deeds, O scorcher of foes, the weak among yogins perish, while the strong are set free.

sanskrit: alpakaś ca yathā rājan vahniḥ śāmyati durbalaḥ ākrānta indhanaiḥ sthūlais tadvad yogo 'balaḥ prabho
english: And as a small, feeble fire dies out, O king, overlaid with great logs of fuel, so does the weak yogin, O lord.

sanskrit: sa eva ca yadā rājan vahnir jātabalaḥ punaḥ samīraṇayutaḥ kṛtsnāṃ dahet kṣipraṃ mahīm api
english: And when that same fire, O king, gathering strength again and joined with the wind, may swiftly burn up the whole earth itself—

sanskrit: tadvaj jātabalo yogī dīptatejā mahābalaḥ antakāla ivādityaḥ kṛtsnaṃ saṃśoṣayej jagat
english: —so the yogin grown strong, blazing with splendor and of mighty power, like the sun at the hour of doom, may parch up the whole world.

sanskrit: durbalaś ca yathā rājan srotasā hriyate naraḥ balahīnas tathā yogo viṣayair hriyate 'vaśaḥ
english: And as a weak man, O king, is swept away by the current, so the feeble yogin is carried off, helpless, by the objects of sense.

sanskrit: tad eva ca yathā sroto viṣṭambhayati vāraṇaḥ tadvad yogabalaṃ labdhvā vyūhate viṣayān bahūn
english: But as an elephant holds back that very current, so, having gained the strength of Yoga, the yogin marshals and sets at naught the many objects of sense.

sanskrit: viśanti cāvaśāḥ pārtha yogā yogabalānvitāḥ prajāpatīn ṛṣīn devān mahābhūtāni ceśvarāḥ
english: And the yogins, endowed with the strength of Yoga and become lords, enter at will, O Pārtha, into the Prajāpatis, the seers, the gods, and the great elements.
